channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Criticizes Emergency Services After Teenager's Death
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President has issued a severe reprimand to the Minister of Emergency Situations for significant shortcomings in organizing rescue operations. This follows the tragic death of a 14-year-old who froze to death after getting lost in the Ala-Archa gorge. Several high-ranking officials have been dismissed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes New Climate Partnership Model for Central Asia
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has proposed a new climate integration model for Central Asia to address shared challenges like glacier melt and water scarcity. The initiative focuses on information exchange, technological cooperation, and financial support, including early warning systems and green financing mechanisms.

item.title: Tajikistan to Chair CSTO in 2027, President Rahmon Outlines Priorities
item.description: Tajikistan will assume the chairmanship of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) in 2027. President Emomali Rahmon stated that efforts will focus on strengthening regional security, enhancing inter-parliamentary cooperation, and expanding military-technical and economic collaboration among member states.

item.title: Head of Demokrat.uz Sentenced to 10.3 Years in Prison
item.description: The head of Demokrat.uz has been sentenced to 10.3 years in prison. Blogger Aziz G'oipnazarov, who was involved in extortion with him, also received a court verdict. Further details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: New Emergency Medical Aid Station to be Built in Petropavlovsk
item.description: A new building for the emergency medical aid station will be constructed in Petropavlovsk, North Kazakhstan region, following a presidential directive. 5.9 billion tenge has been allocated, including approximately 800 million tenge for medical equipment. Construction is planned for completion by December 2027.

item.title: Canada bars Russian athletes from 2027 World Junior Hockey Championship
item.description: Canada has announced it will not allow Russian athletes to participate in the 2027 World Junior Hockey Championship, despite holding valid visas. The decision, citing Russia's war in Ukraine, maintains Canada's firm stance. This comes after the Court of Arbitration for Sport mandated the IIHF to allow Russian teams back into international competitions from 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan to plant forests along roads to combat dust storms
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to plant forests along all roads, both for vehicles and trains, from 2026 to 2035. This "Green Shield of Central Asia" initiative aims to reduce the impact of dust storms, protect soil from wind erosion, and increase green spaces. The project, covering 40,000 hectares, was proposed by Kazakhstan and supported by Central Asian nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Customs Punishes 29 Employees for Violations in IMEI Registration
item.description: Twenty-nine customs officers in Uzbekistan have been disciplined for violations related to mobile device registration and IMEI codes between 2025 and 2026. The Customs Committee conducted 21 internal investigations, resulting in disciplinary actions for 29 employees and preventive talks with 67 others. Some cases also led to criminal proceedings.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Calls for Easier Access to Climate Finance for Mountain Countries
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet chairman, Adylbek Kasymaliev, urged the international community to simplify access to climate finance for developing mountain countries and reduce administrative barriers. Speaking at the COP31 summit in Antalya, he highlighted the gap between the needs of mountain countries for climate adaptation funding and available international support.

item.title: Osh Mayor Meets with Residents to Address Concerns
item.description: Osh Mayor Janarbek Akaev met with residents of the Sulaiman-Too municipal district to hear their issues. Residents raised concerns regarding children's playgrounds, heating systems, public transport schedules, land disputes, and gas and electricity supply. The mayor pledged to address these problems.

item.title: US Offers $20 Million Reward for Information on Iran's Nuclear Program
item.description: The U.S. State Department has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information regarding Iran's nuclear program, including details on facilities, equipment, and personnel. This initiative falls under the 'Rewards for Justice' program. The announcement comes as the IAEA reported Iran enriching uranium to 60% purity, close to weapons-grade levels.

item.title: Uzbekistan's First Lady Proposes Initiatives for Global 'Zero Waste' Alliance
item.description: Uzbekistan's First Lady, Ziroat Mirziyoyeva, participated in a high-level meeting in Antalya, announcing the creation of the Global 'Zero Waste' Alliance. The alliance aims to unite spouses of heads of state to promote resource conservation and waste reduction. She proposed initiatives for environmental education and supporting youth-led ecological projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan to End State Pension Contributions for Mothers on Childcare Leave
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will cease state budget contributions to pensions for mothers on childcare leave. While 10% of childcare payments will still be deducted for pension contributions, the government will no longer cover the difference to maintain the full pension amount. This change aims to streamline pension system payments.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Higher Price Increases for Domestic Food Products Than Imports
item.description: In October 2026, wholesale food prices in Kazakhstan rose by 9% year-on-year. Domestic products saw a 13% increase, while goods from CIS countries rose by 5.8% and others by 1.2%. Processed vegetables, confectionery, chocolate, meat, and dairy products experienced significant price hikes, with only sugar and fruits showing a decrease.

item.title: Tens of Thousands Protest Cost of Living and Housing Shortages in Spain
item.description: Tens of thousands protested rising living costs and housing shortages across Spain on November 11, during the country's first nationwide strike in 14 years. While organizers estimated 600,000 participants, police reported 120,000 in Madrid. Protests in Barcelona ended in riots, with at least 52 arrests nationwide.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Reform Social Payments System Starting 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor announced changes to the procedure for assigning certain social payments, effective 2027. State support for vulnerable citizens, pensions, and benefits for the elderly will be maintained. The principle of targeted support will be strengthened, considering the family's specific circumstances.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan in Talks with Over 20 Countries on Pension Coverage
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has enabled voluntary pension contributions for citizens working abroad via the 'Tunduk' app. The country has existing pension agreements with China, Turkey, and South Korea, and an EAEU agreement. Negotiations are underway with over 20 nations, including Austria and Germany, to facilitate cross-border pension portability.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Early Childhood Development Policy Presented in Bangkok
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's experience in early childhood development and preschool education was presented at an international session in Bangkok. The Minister of Education stated that over 55% of children in the country are covered by early development services. The session discussed expanding access to preschool education and developing inclusive conditions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Identify Over 40 Criminal Groups Negatively Influencing Youth
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs reported identifying over 40 criminal groups that negatively influence young people. Police conducted over two thousand preventive measures in educational institutions this year. Measures are being taken to protect schoolchildren and students from extortion, with four groups involved in such crimes against minors being shut down.

item.title: First Natural Saxaul Sprouts Appear in Aral Sea Desert Following Reforestation Efforts
item.description: The first natural saxaul sprouts have appeared in the desert on the dried bed of the Aral Sea, where saplings have been planted since 2021. Over 3,440 tons of saxaul seeds and other salt-tolerant plants have been sown, with over 53 million saxaul seedlings planted. This initiative aims to restore vegetation cover and create conditions for livestock development.

item.title: President Tokayev Outlines Kazakhstan's Key Development Priorities in New Historical Era Address
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address, 'Kazakhstan's Key Priorities in a New Historical Era,' has defined the country's future development path. The document, released ahead of the 35th anniversary of Independence, outlines important tasks and their implementation strategies. It emphasizes the responsibility of state bodies and law enforcement agencies.

item.title: Tajikistan to Receive $750,000 for Invasive Species Management System
item.description: Tajikistan will receive $750,000 to establish a national system for managing invasive alien species that threaten local ecosystems. The project, presented at the COP17 conference, is part of the NBSAP Accelerator Action Account. Tajikistan is among five countries selected for this initial funding, with the project aiming to identify priority species, assess risks, and develop an action program.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Needs Up to $25 Billion for Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan requires an estimated $20-25 billion over the next decade for climate change adaptation and resilience, according to the Minister of Natural Resources, Ecology, and Technical Supervision. This funding, detailed in the country's updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0), aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and adapt to climate change impacts by 2035.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Investigates 'Enbek' Enterprise Management
item.description: The National Security Committee of Kazakhstan has initiated a pre-trial investigation into the management of the Republican State Enterprise 'Enbek'. Details of the investigation have not been disclosed. The announcement was made by the committee, with further information pending.

item.title: Kazakhstan-linked Hackers Stole Documents from Tajikistan's State Systems Using AI
item.description: A hacking group, Silent Lynx, allegedly linked to Kazakhstan, infiltrated Tajikistan's electronic document management system, stealing over 2,000 documents including sensitive defense and national security materials. They reportedly used AI, specifically the Hermes platform, to automate reconnaissance and data exfiltration.

item.title: New Dairy Processing Plant Under Construction in Kyrgyzstan with $7.7 Million Investment
item.description: A new plant for processing milk and producing dairy products is being built in Kyrgyzstan, attracting an investment of $7.7 million. The project, 'Nurukura Pro' LLC, is expected to increase domestic milk processing volumes, create jobs, and produce export-oriented dairy products meeting international quality standards.

item.title: Kazakhstan Debates Strengthening Local Assemblies (Maslikhats) Post-2022 Reforms
item.description: Following the January 2022 events, Kazakhstan is preparing for new elections to its local assemblies (maslikhats). Experts hold differing views on the effectiveness of reforms aimed at empowering these bodies, with some arguing for further review of local self-governance structures despite changes to electoral systems.

item.title: Samruk-Kazyna Management Denies, Yet Refuses to Confirm Detention Reports
item.description: Information has emerged online regarding the detention of Samruk-Kazyna's management. The company has neither confirmed nor denied these reports, stating they are withholding comment until official information is received from authorized bodies and all circumstances are clarified. Official confirmation is currently absent.

item.title: Almaty Authorities Uncover Embezzlement of 945 Million Tenge in Science Projects
item.description: The Anti-Corruption Agency's department in Almaty has concluded an investigation into the director of "Bal halal" LLP, suspected of embezzling 945 million tenge allocated for scientific development commercialization. The company received 1.15 billion tenge for four projects but allegedly used funds for non-compliant equipment, leading to significant financial loss.

item.title: President Signs Law on New State Awards
item.description: The President has signed a new law concerning state awards. This legislative act introduces a framework for the establishment and awarding of new state honors. Further details regarding the specific types of awards or the criteria for their bestowal are not provided in the source text.

item.title: New Tashkent to Establish Separate City Administration Appointed by President
item.description: A dedicated city administration will be created for the developing New Tashkent, with its head appointed directly by the president. This new structure, comprising 14 staff members, will manage the future city's affairs even before its official establishment as a separate administrative unit. The administration will have independent decision-making powers over territories assigned to the New Tashkent Construction Directorate.

item.title: CSTO Discusses Unified Biosecurity System for Member States
item.description: The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) discussed the formation of a unified biosecurity system for its member states. Anna Popova of Rospotrebnadzor highlighted the increasing threats from infectious diseases, artificial biological threats, and potential bioterrorism. She emphasized the need for a unified system due to shared epidemiological risks and growing threats from migration, climate change, and biotechnology advancements.

item.title: Central Asia to Receive 200 Million Euros for Climate-Resilient Landscapes
item.description: A regional program, 'Climate-Resilient Landscapes in Central Asia' (CLiCA), will receive 200 million euros for development. The program's strategic importance for regional cooperation and climate resilience was highlighted by Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Natural Resources, Akyl Toktobayev. He thanked Germany for its support, emphasizing the program's significance for Kyrgyzstan's mountainous ecosystems and the entire Central Asian region's water, food, and ecological security.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Apprehend Four Groups Involved in Extorting Students
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs continues systematic work to prevent crime among youth. Over 40 groups influencing youth negatively have been identified this year, with over 100 individuals detained. Four groups specifically targeting students for extortion have been stopped.

item.title: Kazakhstan Science Fund Embezzlement Scheme Involving Pasta Projects Revealed
item.description: Kazakhstan's financial monitoring agency has concluded an investigation into the director of 'Bal halal' for embezzling funds from the 'Science Fund'. The company received 1.15 billion tenge for innovative pasta projects but allegedly used a related company to divert 736.4 million tenge.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Secures 60,000 Signatures for Re-election Bid
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's incumbent President Sadyr Japarov has collected 60,000 signatures, double the minimum required, for his candidacy in the upcoming elections. The Central Election Commission will make the final registration decision after verifying documents and requirements. The nomination period ends November 13.

item.title: Uzbek President's Son-in-Law Involved in Major Business Deal for Real Estate
item.description: Oybek Tursunov, son-in-law of Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, has been approved for a large transaction to purchase real estate valued at over 98 billion Uzbek soums. This deal raises questions about preferential treatment and the influence of presidential family ties in business.

item.title: Kazakhstan Faces Potential Economic Downturn in Some Regions, Expert Warns
item.description: An oil and gas expert suggests Kazakhstan may be experiencing an economic downturn in certain regions, though the impact varies across the country. While high oil prices initially delayed the crisis, recent statistics show declining industrial production in several oblasts. Migration towards larger cities is also increasing as some regions see population decreases.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan Launch Test Freight Services on New Railway Line
item.description: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan have commenced test freight operations on the new "Darboza – Maktaaral" railway line, with the first shipment of Kazakh coal sent in October. The route is expected to fully launch in December, aiming to alleviate pressure on the existing "Saryagash – Tashkent" section and boost transport capacity.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks Third Globally in Land Restoration Area
item.description: Kazakhstan has achieved third place worldwide in the area of land undergoing restoration, according to the UN's "Nature's Comeback" report. The country is undertaking restoration efforts on 8.13 million hectares, surpassing all nations except China and Mongolia. This initiative aims to prevent further land degradation and preserve soil fertility.
